lines.trans: I am repeating one more time for all of you.
Today is an important banquet for an oil magnate.
If he does not like it, we will be ruined.
Wait a second, what is this awful stench?
What is this on your table, guys?
Did someone boil socks? Why does it smell like this?
Is this some cheap cafeteria we have here?
Dima, do not worry, we will fix everything right now.
Pull yourselves together, we will still manage to cook everything.
First of all we need to urgently turn on the lights.

examples.trans: Nothing, we have already cooked everything.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'чало'). Common neuter noun meaning 'beginning' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Для начала нам надо срочно включить свет.
examples.trans: First of all we need to urgently turn on the lights.

examples.text: Мне нужно сначала деньги в ресторан вложить?
examples.trans: Do I need to invest money in the restaurant first?

examples.text: Это только начало.
examples.trans: It's only the beginning.

meanings.en: must, need to, it is necessary
meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Лёва поставит мясо в духовку надолго.
examples.trans: Lyova will put the meat in the oven for a long time.

examples.text: Мне надо срочно проверить тут электричество.
examples.trans: I need to urgently check the electricity here.

examples.text: Электричество надо срочно проверить.
examples.trans: The electricity needs checking urgently.

meanings.en: urgently, right away; predicative: it is urgent
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'рочно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Шеф просто дал мне срочную работу.
examples.trans: Chef just gave me urgent work.

examples.text: Мне надо срочно проверить тут электричество.
examples.trans: I need to urgently check the electricity here.

examples.text: Электричество надо срочно проверить.
examples.trans: The electricity needs checking urgently.

включить.gloss: to turn on, to plug in

meanings.en: to switch on, to plug in
meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to turn on, to plug in', paired with 'включать'.

examples.text: Для начала нам надо срочно включить свет.
examples.trans: First of all we need to urgently turn on the lights.

examples.text: Сейчас включу.
examples.trans: I'll plug it in right now.

examples.text: Включи, пожалуйста, чайник.
examples.trans: Switch on the kettle, please.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'light; electricity' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Что у нас случилось со светом?
examples.trans: What happened to our lights?

examples.text: Для начала нам надо срочно включить свет.
examples.trans: First of all we need to urgently turn on the lights.

examples.text: Включи свет.
examples.trans: Turn on the light.

meanings.note: Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'building' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Здание полностью обесточено, чинить будут два дня.
examples.trans: The building has no power at all, repairs will take two days.

examples.text: На огромной скорости машина врезалась в здание!
examples.trans: At huge speed the car crashed into the building!

examples.text: Это старое красивое здание.
examples.trans: This is an old, beautiful building.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'лностью').

examples.text: Отличная идея, я полностью одобряю.
examples.trans: Great idea, I completely approve.

examples.text: Здание полностью обесточено, чинить будут два дня.
examples.trans: The building has no power at all, repairs will take two days.

examples.text: Марина Сергеевна полностью закрыла долг.
examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna has paid off the debt in full.

meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'есточить'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('cut off from power').

examples.text: Шеф говорит, что это очень обесточить выбор.
examples.trans: The chef says that this is a very cut off from power choice.

examples.text: У нас сегодня просто обесточить день в ресторане.
examples.trans: We are having a simply cut off from power day at the restaurant today.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'fix', paired with 'починить'.

examples.text: Ну хорошо, тогда давай чини при мне.
examples.trans: Alright then, go ahead and fix it in front of me.

examples.text: Здание полностью обесточено, чинить будут два дня.
examples.trans: The building has no power at all, repairs will take two days.

examples.text: Сейчас будешь чинить трубу.
examples.trans: Now you're going to fix the pipe.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.

examples.text: Хозяин должен быть сильный и уверенный.
examples.trans: The owner must be strong and confident.

examples.text: У меня есть машинка.
examples.trans: I have a toy car.

examples.text: Детство было трудное.
examples.trans: Childhood was hard.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian cardinal or ordinal numeral meaning 'two', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Здание полностью обесточено, чинить будут два дня.
examples.trans: The building has no power at all, repairs will take two days.

examples.text: Через две недели.
examples.trans: In two weeks.

examples.text: Два дома.
examples.trans: Two houses.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'day' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Там были все мои деньги!
examples.trans: All my money was in there!

examples.text: Там были все мои деньги, понимаешь?
examples.trans: All my money was in there, do you understand?

examples.text: Деньги были на наш второй этаж.
examples.trans: The money was for our second floor.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('sad').

examples.text: Ребята, а что вы все такие грустные?
examples.trans: Guys, why are you all looking so sad?

examples.text: Почему ты такой грустный?
examples.trans: Why are you so sad?

examples.text: Это грустная история.
examples.trans: It's a sad story.
